identity.title: LLM DNA: Tracing Model Evolution via Functional Representations

problem.claim: LLM evolutionary relationships through fine-tuning, distillation, and adaptation are often undocumented or unclear, complicating model management.

gap.claim: Existing approaches are constrained by task specificity, fixed model sets, or strict tokenizer and architecture assumptions.

contributions.claim: Defines LLM DNA as a low-dimensional, bi-Lipschitz representation of functional behavior, and establishes its existence together with inheritance and genetic determinism properties.
Derives a general, scalable, training-free pipeline for extracting LLM DNA.
Uses DNA comparisons and phylogenetic algorithms to analyze relationships and evolutionary structure across LLMs.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish their approach by mathematically grounding model comparison in a low-dimensional functional representation designed to avoid the stated task, model-set, tokenizer, and architecture limitations.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report experiments across 305 LLMs in which DNA aligns with prior studies on limited subsets and performs superiorly or competitively across various tasks.
The authors report that DNA comparisons uncover previously undocumented relationships among LLMs.
The authors report that an evolutionary tree aligns with encoder-decoder to decoder-only shifts, reflects temporal progression, and reveals distinct evolutionary speeds across LLM families.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper frames the undocumented evolutionary landscape of millions of LLMs as a model-management problem.
It identifies task-, model-set-, tokenizer-, and architecture-dependent constraints in existing methods.
It defines LLM DNA as a low-dimensional bi-Lipschitz functional representation and states inheritance, genetic determinism, and existence results.
It derives a scalable training-free extraction pipeline, then reports results across 305 LLMs and uses DNA for relationship discovery and phylogenetic analysis.

source_observation.claim: The abstract connects a formal representation, a training-free extraction pipeline, and downstream phylogenetic analysis in one progression.

lessons.interpretation: A representation becomes more persuasive when its formal properties are linked to a concrete, scalable procedure and a management-relevant use.
lessons.application: When proposing a model-comparison representation, pair its definition and guarantees with an explicit extraction workflow and a downstream structural analysis.
lessons.exception: This framing may be unsuitable when the representation is intended only for a narrowly defined task or lacks a meaningful downstream use.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the various tasks, baselines, metrics, or conditions behind the superior or competitive performance claim.
Details supporting the stated proofs, existence result, and alignment with prior studies are not provided.
The validation basis for previously undocumented relationships and the phylogenetic tree is unspecified.
